public_brief: You are building the username field for a website signup form. Implement validate_username(username), which receives exactly what the user typed into the field and answers one question: may this name be registered? Return True when the name can be accepted as-is and False when it must be rejected. The validator sits in front of account creation, so treat it as a gate for anything the site would not want as a username. Keep it a pure function: no printing, no prompting, no filesystem or network access. Graders call it directly with ordinary names and with messy values - odd types, padded text, reserved-sounding words - and compare what comes back, so every input path needs a defined answer.
entry_contract: Implement validate_username(username) taking one positional argument of any type and returning a strict bool (True or False) for every input.

hidden_spec.rule: The name must be between 3 and 20 characters long, counting the string exactly as typed; shorter or longer is rejected.
Only ASCII letters, digits, and underscore are allowed; spaces, hyphens, dots, accented or non-Latin characters, and emoji make it False.
The name must begin with a letter, never a digit or an underscore.

The reserved names admin, administrator, root, moderator, support, and system are rejected case-insensitively on exact match, while longer names that merely contain one of them (e.g. adminuser) are allowed.
Leading or trailing whitespace makes the name False exactly as typed; the validator never trims before judging.
At most two identical characters may appear consecutively; a run of three or more of the same character is rejected as keyboard mashing.
None or any non-string argument returns False and never raises; the form always gets a boolean answer.

answer_sheet.answer: Three to twenty characters inclusive. Shorter looks like a stub, longer clutters the roster.
Letters, digits, underscore only - ASCII. No spaces, hyphens, dots, accents, or emoji.
Must open with a letter. A digit or underscore up front reads machine-generated.
Six reserved names, exact match, case-insensitive. adminuser or roots still passes - they aren't the reserved word.
Padded input fails as typed. We never trim for them; sloppy entry is the user's problem.
Two of the same character in a row is fine. Three or more is keyboard mashing, so reject.
Anything that isn't text comes back False - here we answer, we never throw. Opposite of the phone task on purpose.
Out of scope - this validator judges usernames only; password strength lives elsewhere.
Out of scope - no database lookup; pure predicate on the string. Duplicate handling is the signup service's job.

provenance.derivation: Rules derived from mainstream web-signup username conventions (bounded length, ASCII alnum-plus-underscore charset, letter-first rule, reserved-name blocklists, no-trim policy, repeat-run limits), not from any WiseCounsil design document.
